decisions.decision: Bespoke illustrated cup/waffle glyph system (src/components/brand/DrinkGlyphs.tsx) instead of stock icons or missing product photos. Recolored per product using only existing brand tokens (cyan, gold, red/terracotta ramp) — tonal variation within one palette, never a new hue per flavor. Hero rewritten with asymmetric layout, floating promo/flavor badge chips, and copy tied specifically to the crown/king brand motif ('Crowned in boba', 'Visit the throne room') rather than generic food-delivery copy. Added a faint SVG-turbulence grain texture (.bg-grain) on dark hero/menu surfaces for tactile depth without gradients or glassmorphism. Single-branch 'Visit' section redesigned as one composed panel (address/hours/phone) rather than a multi-branch list pattern applied to one item.
decisions.rejected: 21st hosted search/generate (get_inspiration HTTP 401, no API key in this environment) and the ui-ux-pro-max generic 'Bakery/Cafe'-style design-system suggestion (green/pink 'Liquid Glass' — conflicted with the real brand's established terracotta/teal/gold identity and the explicit 'avoid glassmorphism, don't scatter colors' constraints).

decisions.decision: Replaced the bespoke illustrated cup/waffle glyph system (DrinkGlyphs.tsx, deleted) with real photography pulled from the brand's own TikTok (@bobaking_gh): real cups, real interior, real hands sealing drinks at the counter. User feedback on the illustrated version was explicit — it still read as generic/AI-templated despite matching the palette. 15 photos were fetched and visually vetted one-by-one before use (one video-thumbnail frame was an inappropriate freeze-frame of a person and was discarded; a low-res announcement graphic was discarded). Every remaining photo shows the actual product, staff, or storefront. Restructured every section around photography: full-bleed photo hero (was split text+SVG-illustration), a floating polaroid-style second photo for depth, a photo-card menu grid (was flat color-tint + icon tiles), a new 'Behind the counter' two-photo editorial section (did not exist before), and a photo-backdrop Visit section (was a plain list). taro-milk-tea's only available photo is a promo poster with a baked-in stale price (₵45 vs. the real ₵65) — since the source is portrait and every card shape here is wider, CSS object-position can only crop it vertically, so there is no framing that hides the wrong price while keeping the cup visible; it and brown-sugar-boba-milk-tea (no photo exists) render as deliberate color-block typographic tiles instead, which also doubles as a rhythm break against seven photo tiles.
decisions.rejected: Keeping the illustrated glyph system with different colors/shapes (would not have addressed the actual 'looks AI' complaint, which was about illustration-vs-photography, not palette); using the taro promo poster as-is (visible price would contradict the real listed price on the same card).
